drhp.business: The company is an integrated turnkey construction service provider having pan India presence with expertise in construction design, engineering, procurement, construction and project management. It also provides construction allied services such as mechanical & electrical, plumbing, fire fighting, heating, ventilation and air conditioning.
drhp.expansion: The Company is initiating a separate ERP system to support anticipated growth opportunities in diverse fields across various geographical locations; the system is in advanced stage of closure and is likely to be functional during Q2 of FY2026-27. To further strengthen operational capabilities, the Board has augmented the management team by inducting experienced professionals across various levels of the organization.

litigation.note: Creditors initiated insolvency proceedings against the Company under the IBC, 2016 in 2021 and the matter was referred to the NCLT; with promoters' commitment to reviving the Company, a settlement was reached with creditors and the petition was withdrawn under Section 124 of the IBC, 2016 pursuant to an NCLT order dated 5th January 2024. Owing to the concluded insolvency proceedings, the Company remains unable to secure Non-Fund Based (NFB) facilities required to support operations, adversely impacting profitability via increased creditor payment terms. Separately, Delhi South Extension Car Park Ltd (subsidiary) has certain claims against Delhi Municipal Corporation for cancellation of a concession, under consideration by the corporation.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Owing to the concluded insolvency proceedings, the Company remains unable to secure NFB facilities required to support its operations, adversely impacting profitability via increased creditor payment terms; this is expected to continue affecting performance until fully resolved.
- The Company incurred losses in previous years due to contractual mismatches and delays in project closures; in 2021 creditors initiated insolvency proceedings under the IBC, 2016, referred to the NCLT; a settlement was reached and the petition withdrawn in January 2024, but downstream effects (NFB unavailability) persist.
- Working capital cycle has been elongated mainly due to stretched receivables, affecting cash flow across companies in the sector, forcing many to draw full banking limits or restructure facilities.
- The sector's lengthy dispute resolution mechanism is a major factor affecting cash flows of construction companies.
- Shortage of labour has become a threat as the industry depends majorly on labour for its sustainability.
- Policy bottlenecks, slow clearance of projects and rising inflation have dampened private-sector sentiment and stifled capital-expenditure investments, though a high-level committee has been constituted for speedy clearance of stalled projects.
- The Company identifies Business, Financial, Commodity, Exchange Rate, Market, Legal, and Political risk as risks faced by construction projects generally, reviewed by the Audit Committee under its risk management framework.
- Risks are weighted to the downside from the uncertainty around a potentially more challenging and inflationary trade environment, which could affect the otherwise favourable 2026 infrastructure outlook.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- The Company is eying to foray into high margin and bulk order jobs, not only in its conventional portfolio but also in diversified jobs.
- Management remains focused on improving operational efficiency, strengthening the order book, and creating sustainable value for all stakeholders.
- The Board has augmented the management team by inducting experienced professionals across various levels of the organization to enhance business development efforts, improve project execution efficiency, and facilitate timely completion of projects.
- Management is exploring the possibility of closing subsidiaries …
